chunks: Von ihm, von an-Nadr ibn Suwayd, von 'Asim ibn Humayd, von Muhammad ibn Muslim, der sagte:
Ich fragte Abu Ja'far (friede sei mit ihm): Tritt ein Mann ohne Ihram nach Mekka ein? Er sagte: "Nein, außer für einen Kranken oder einen, der an einer Bauchkrankheit (Ruhr/Magenbeschwerden) leidet."

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِحْرَامٍ: Ritual consecration state for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.بَطَنٌ: Belly ailment, specifically dysentery or stomach issues

ai.seo_question: Can a person enter Mecca without ihram if they are sick?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the obligation of *ihram* for entering Mecca, distinguishing between the general rule and specific medical exemptions. The term 'batn' (stomach ailment) is interpreted by Shia jurists to include conditions like dysentery where the ritual acts of *ihram* would cause undue hardship, reflecting the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in Shia fiqh.
